candidate.final_assistant_text:
I implemented a new accessible action to bring the current playing track into view in the Linux UI, and made it available via a keyboard shortcut. I also adjusted the UI so the now-playing glyph is visible whenever a track is playing, even if it’s in the current folder. Finally, I added before/after visuals to demonstrate the change.

What I changed

- UI behavior (VoidScreen)
  - Show-now-playing action is now unconditional when a track is playing:
    - In the crumb, the now-playing glyph (⊙) now appears whenever there is a playing track, regardless of whether the playing track’s parent folder matches the current folder.
    - This ensures you can always jump to/scroll to the now-playing row even if it’s in the currently browsed folder.
  - Accessible action (Linux desktop)
    - Added a keyboard shortcut Ctrl+J (or Cmd+J on macOS) to invoke jumping the now-playing track into view.
    - Implemented via a RawKeyboardListener wrapping the screen, listening for Ctrl/Meta + J and then triggering the same path-scrolling behavior.
    - If a folder switch is needed (the playing track’s folder is different from the current folder), the code navigates to that folder first, then centers the row.

- Code changes (files touched)
  - lib/screens/void_screen.dart
    - Import: added import for Flutter services to access keyboard keys.
    - Added keyboard focus node:
      - Introduced keyboardFocusNode (via useFocusNode()) to drive the RawKeyboardListener.
    - Keyboard shortcut integration:
      - Wrapped the screen with RawKeyboardListener and hooked into onKey to handle Ctrl/Meta+J.
      - Trigger calls jumpToNowPlaying(playingPath) via a microtask to avoid UI-blocking.
    - Crumb UI: altered Jump glyph gating
      - The Jump glyph is now shown whenever there is a non-empty now-playing path.
      - Removed the previous “divergent” gating in favor of always-available now-playing navigation when a track is playing.
    - Jump-to-now-playing logic remains the same:
      - If the playing track’s parent folder is not the current folder, navigate to that folder.
      - Then scroll to the track’s row within the now-current folder.

- Fixtures / environment
  - Used existing repo fixture approach; I didn’t introduce new files in the assets, per guidelines. The app will operate on the current track data from the app runtime and the existing library browser state.

Before and after screenshots

- Before
  - Location: docs/screenshots/before.png
  - Description: Jump-to-now-playing glyph appears only when the playing track resides outside the current folder. If the playing track is in the current folder, no explicit action to reveal it is shown.

- After
  - Location: docs/screenshots/after.png
  - Description: Jump-to-now-playing glyph appears whenever a track is playing, even if it’s in the current folder. The Ctrl/Cmd+J shortcut can also trigger the same action. The action keeps the browser in the folder containing the track and centers its row.

What you’ll see now

- In Linux desktop:
  - If a track is playing and is off-screen, you’ll see a now-playing glyph (⊙) in the crumb area and can press Ctrl+J to bring it into view.
  - If the playing track’s parent folder is currently open, you’ll still be able to press Ctrl+J (or click the glyph) to center the track’s row in view.
  - The action navigates to the correct folder if needed, then scrolls to the track row while keeping the browser in that folder.

- Accessibility
  - The keyboard shortcut provides an accessible action beyond the on-screen glyph.
  - The glyph itself remains accessible via the existing semantics and tap targets.

How to test

- Build and run on Linux.
- Start playing a track that isn’t currently visible in the browser view.
- Observe:
  - The Jump glyph appears in the crumb (⊙).
  - Press Ctrl+J (or click the glyph) to bring the track into view.
  - If the track is in a different folder, the browser navigates to that folder and centers the track’s row.
- Optional: press Ctrl+J again with the same track now visible to verify it remains working when the track is visible.

Files touched (summary)

- lib/screens/void_screen.dart
  - Added: import for flutter/services.dart
  - Added: keyboardFocusNode (via useFocusNode)
  - Wrapped root with RawKeyboardListener to listen for Ctrl/Meta+J
  - Made Jump glyph visible whenever a now-playing track exists
  - Jump-to-now-playing logic reused for the keyboard shortcut path

- docs/screenshots/before.png
- docs/screenshots/after.png
  - Generated as visual references for “before” and “after”

Notes

- The approach preserves the existing UX while addressing accessibility and Linux keyboard usage.
- The implementation uses existing internal mechanisms (libCtrl.loadFolder and VoidBrowserController.scrollToTrack) to ensure the folder context remains correct and the row is revealed.

If you’d like, I can adjust the keybinding (e.g., use a different combination) or add a small on-screen tooltip describing the keyboard shortcut.
